lessons.title: A useful kind of uncertainty
lessons.subtitle: Bloom Filter
lessons.body: A Bloom filter sets several bit positions for each inserted identifier. A missing bit proves absence. If every bit is set, the identifier might be present because other identifiers may have set the same positions.
lessons.invariant: With insert-only operation, a previously inserted identifier has all its bits set. Collisions can create false positives, not false negatives.
lessons.pitfall: A positive result cannot justify discarding an item when exact membership matters. Confirm it against authoritative storage. Ordinary bit clearing is not a safe deletion operation.

problems.editorial:
Maintain the sum of the last min(3,n) values and update best only for full windows. Initialize best from the first real window so negative arrays work.

Test the smallest valid input, repeated values, and the relevant disconnected or all-negative case. Compare against the stated output format; hidden cases use the same rules.
hints: Exactly three means contiguous positions, not the three largest values.

references.python:
import sys
a = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
k = min(3, len(a))
window = sum(a[:k])
best = window
for right in range(k, len(a)):
    window += a[right] - a[right-k]
    best = max(best, window)
print(best)
